What is a chemical reaction? (রাসায়নিক বিক্রিয়া)

A chemical reaction is a change in which one or more substances change into new substances with new properties. The starting substances are called reactants (বিক্রিয়ক) and the new substances formed are called products (উৎপাদ).

How to read an equation

Reactants → Products

The arrow (→) means “changes into”. A balanced equation has the same number of each kind of atom on both sides. Always check the balance before you learn an equation.

Symbols to know: (s) solid, (l) liquid, (g) gas, (aq) in water. Heat is often written as Δ over the arrow.

How each type is taught

Each of the 5 types below has a definition, a general form, 5 balanced examples, important points and real-life uses. The comparison table and practice questions are at the end.

One trick to identify any reaction

Count first, then look for clues. Many → one is addition. One → many is decomposition. Burning in oxygen with heat and light is combustion. One element pushing another out is substitution. Acid + base → salt + water is neutralization.

1

Many join to make one

Addition Reaction (সংযোজন বিক্রিয়া)

Also called Combination or Synthesis reaction

Definition

A reaction in which two or more substances join together to form only one new substance is called an addition (combination) reaction.

General form
A + B → AB | X + Y + Z → XYZ

Important examples — learn all 5

2Mg + O2 → 2MgO
Magnesium burns with a bright white light and forms white magnesium oxide powder.
CaO + H2O → Ca(OH)2
Quicklime (calcium oxide) + water → slaked lime. Heat comes out and the mixture hisses.
H2 + Cl2 → 2HCl
Hydrogen + chlorine (in sunlight) → hydrogen chloride gas.
C + O2 → CO2
Carbon (charcoal) joins with oxygen to form carbon dioxide.
NH3 + HCl → NH4Cl
Ammonia + hydrogen chloride → ammonium chloride. Dense white fumes are seen.

Characteristics / important points

  • Two or more reactants, but only one product. This is the easiest way to spot it.
  • It is the opposite of decomposition (Section 4).
  • The reactants may be elements (Mg, O2) or compounds (CaO, H2O) — both are allowed.
  • Many addition reactions give out heat, for example quicklime with water.
Real life / textbook Making slaked lime for whitewashing walls (CaO + water). The white-fume test with NH3 and HCl is a favourite scholarship question.
2

Burning in oxygen

Combustion Reaction (দহন বিক্রিয়া)

Definition

A reaction in which a substance burns in oxygen (air) and gives out heat and light, forming an oxide, is called a combustion reaction.

General form
Substance + O2 → Oxide + heat + light
For a fuel containing carbon and hydrogen: Fuel + O2 → CO2 + H2O + heat + light

Important examples — learn all 5

CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O
Methane (natural gas) burns fully. This is the gas-stove reaction.
C + O2 → CO2
Charcoal / coal burns in enough air to form carbon dioxide.
2Mg + O2 → 2MgO
Magnesium burns with a dazzling white flame. Also an addition reaction.
S + O2 → SO2
Sulfur burns with a blue flame and forms choking sulfur dioxide gas.
2H2 + O2 → 2H2O
Hydrogen burns with a pop sound and forms water.

Characteristics / important points

  • Oxygen is a must. No oxygen, no combustion.
  • Heat and light always come out — combustion always gives out energy.
  • Three things are needed to start burning: fuel, oxygen and heat (the fire triangle).
  • Some combustion reactions are also addition reactions (Mg, C, S above), because only one oxide is formed.
  • If air is too little, burning is incomplete and poisonous carbon monoxide (CO) can form — never burn fuel in a closed room.
Real life / textbook Cooking gas, candles, wood and coal burning, and petrol in engines are all combustion. Fire extinguishers work by cutting off oxygen or cooling the fuel.
3

One pushes another out

Substitution Reaction (প্রতিস্থাপন বিক্রিয়া)

Also called Displacement reaction

Definition

A reaction in which a more reactive element takes the place of (displaces) a less reactive element from its compound is called a substitution (displacement) reaction.

General form
AB + C → AC + B
C is more reactive than B

Important examples — learn all 5

Zn + CuSO4 → ZnSO4 + Cu
Zinc is more reactive than copper. The blue colour of copper sulfate slowly fades; brown copper forms.
Fe + CuSO4 → FeSO4 + Cu
An iron nail in blue copper sulfate gets a brown copper coating; the solution turns light green.
Zn + H2SO4 → ZnSO4 + H2↑
Zinc displaces hydrogen from dilute sulfuric acid. Bubbles of hydrogen gas come out.
Mg + 2HCl → MgCl2 + H2↑
Magnesium reacts fast with dilute hydrochloric acid and gives hydrogen gas.
Cu + 2AgNO3 → Cu(NO3)2 + 2Ag
Copper is more reactive than silver, so silver is displaced and the solution turns blue.

Characteristics / important points

  • One element + one compound react, and a new element + new compound are formed.
  • It happens only if the free element is more reactive. Copper cannot displace zinc from ZnSO4 — no reaction.
  • Colour change is a common sign: blue CuSO4 solution fades or turns green.
  • Metals above hydrogen (like Zn, Fe, Mg) displace hydrogen from dilute acids.
Real life / textbook The iron nail in copper sulfate solution is the most common Class 8 practical and scholarship example. Learn the reactivity idea in simple words: stronger pushes out weaker.
4

One breaks into many

Decomposition Reaction (বিয়োজন বিক্রিয়া)

Definition

A reaction in which one compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances is called a decomposition reaction. Heat, light or electricity is usually needed.

General form
AB → A + B | ABC → A + B + C

Important examples — learn all 5

CaCO3 → CaO + CO2heat
Limestone on strong heating gives quicklime + carbon dioxide. Used to make lime and cement.
2H2O → 2H2 + O2electricity
Water splits by electric current (electrolysis) into hydrogen and oxygen.
2HgO → 2Hg + O2heat
Red mercuric oxide on heating gives mercury and oxygen.
2KClO3 → 2KCl + 3O2heat
Potassium chlorate heated (with MnO2 as helper) gives oxygen in the laboratory.
2H2O2 → 2H2O + O2
Hydrogen peroxide slowly breaks down into water and oxygen, faster in light.

Characteristics / important points

  • Only one reactant, but two or more products. This is the opposite of addition.
  • Energy must usually be supplied — by heat, electricity or sunlight. Without it, most compounds do not break.
  • MnO2 in the KClO3 example is a catalyst (অনুঘটক): it speeds up the reaction and is not used up.
  • Do not confuse with substitution: in decomposition there is no free element pushing anything out — the compound simply breaks.
Real life / textbook Heating limestone to make quicklime for cement, electrolysis of water, and baking soda breaking down on heating when a cake is baked — it gives out CO2 gas, which makes the cake rise. The CaCO3 equation is asked again and again in exams.
5

Acid + base = salt + water

Neutralization Reaction (প্রশমন বিক্রিয়া)

Definition

A reaction between an acid (এসিড) and a base (ক্ষার) that forms salt (লবণ) and water is called a neutralization reaction. The acid and the base cancel each other, so the mixture becomes neutral.

General form
Acid + Base → Salt + Water

Important examples — learn all 5

HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H2O
Hydrochloric acid + sodium hydroxide → common salt (sodium chloride) + water. The model example.
H2SO4 + 2KOH → K2SO4 + 2H2O
Sulfuric acid + potassium hydroxide → potassium sulfate + water.
HNO3 + NaOH → NaNO3 + H2O
Nitric acid + sodium hydroxide → sodium nitrate + water.
2HCl + Ca(OH)2 → CaCl2 + 2H2O
Hydrochloric acid + slaked lime → calcium chloride + water.
2HCl + Mg(OH)2 → MgCl2 + 2H2O
Stomach acid + magnesium hydroxide (antacid) → magnesium chloride + water.

Characteristics / important points

  • The products are always salt + water. If water is not formed, it is not neutralization.
  • The sour / bitter effect disappears: the final mixture is neutral when acid and base are in the right amount.
  • Heat comes out during neutralization — the test tube feels warm.
  • An indicator shows the end point: for example, litmus changes colour when the mixture becomes neutral.
  • Too much or too little of one side leaves the mixture acidic or alkaline — amount matters.
Real life / textbook Antacid for acidity in the stomach, toothpaste (mild base) neutralizing acid in the mouth, farmers adding lime to acidic soil, and treating factory waste water before it goes into rivers.

Comparison of All 5 Types — At a Glance

Read one row at a time. In the exam, first count the reactants and products, then use the “easy sign” column.

TypeGeneral formOne exampleEasy sign to spot it
1. Addition(সংযোজন) A + B → AB CaO + H2O → Ca(OH)2 Many reactants, one product
2. Combustion(দহন) Substance + O2 → oxide + heat + light CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O Burning in oxygen; heat + light out
3. Substitution(প্রতিস্থাপন) AB + C → AC + B Zn + CuSO4 → ZnSO4 + Cu More reactive element pushes out a weaker one
4. Decomposition(বিয়োজন) AB → A + B CaCO3 → CaO + CO2 One reactant, many products; needs heat / electricity
5. Neutralization(প্রশমন) Acid + base → salt + water HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H2O Products are always salt + water

Quick revision — say it in 10 seconds each

  • Addition: join → one product.
  • Combustion: burn in O2 → heat + light.
  • Substitution: stronger element takes the place of a weaker one.
  • Decomposition: break → one reactant, many products.
  • Neutralization: acid + base → salt + water.

Do not mix these up: Addition and decomposition are opposites. Combustion needs oxygen and burning — a plain addition with no burning is not combustion. Substitution has a free element on both sides; decomposition has a compound alone on the left.

Practice — Junior Scholarship Style

Try without looking. Then open the answers below. Write the type and one reason for each.

A. Name the reaction type

  1. S + O2 → SO2 (burning)
  2. 2H2O → 2H2 + O2 (electricity passed)
  3. Fe + CuSO4 → FeSO4 + Cu
  4. HNO3 + NaOH → NaNO3 + H2O
  5. NH3 + HCl → NH4Cl

B. Short questions

  1. Why does the blue colour of CuSO4 fade when zinc is added?
  2. Name the salt formed when HCl reacts with NaOH.
  3. What three things are needed for combustion?
  4. Why is CaCO3 → CaO + CO2 not an addition reaction?
  5. How does an antacid help acidity in the stomach? Name the reaction type.
Show answers

1. Combustion (also addition — one oxide formed). 2. Decomposition. 3. Substitution — Fe is more reactive than Cu. 4. Neutralization — acid + base → salt + water. 5. Addition — two reactants, one product.

6. Zinc displaces copper from CuSO4; colourless ZnSO4 forms and copper separates out. 7. Sodium chloride (NaCl). 8. Fuel, oxygen and heat. 9. One reactant breaks into two products — that is decomposition, the opposite of addition. 10. The antacid is a base; it neutralizes extra stomach acid — neutralization.

Exam tips: Always write balanced equations — an unbalanced equation loses marks. Write the Bangla name beside the English name when the question asks for the type. For “identify the reaction” questions, give the type and the reason (one product / salt + water / displacement), not the type alone.
